nodes.name: A conversation is a starting point.
nodes.text: ## A conversation is a starting point.

nodes.name: A useful conversation can settle a naming rule, explain a…
nodes.text: A useful conversation can settle a naming rule, explain a trade-off, or uncover a constraint. But the next person may never see that conversation. The next agent session may start without it.

nodes.name: Move the result into a short, maintained document. Record…
nodes.text: Move the result into a short, maintained document. Record the decision, why it was made, and what would justify changing it. Keep speculation separate from rules the team has accepted. A decision written in two sentences and kept current is worth more than a long transcript nobody rereads.

nodes.name: Put the guidance where the work belongs.
nodes.text: ## Put the guidance where the work belongs.

nodes.name: Use workspace guidance for decisions that apply to…
nodes.text: Use workspace guidance for decisions that apply to everyone. If your workspace uses products, put product guidance beside decisions shared across related projects. Keep project-specific instructions with the project that needs them.

nodes.name: A web repository and an iOS repository can belong to the…
nodes.text: A web repository and an iOS repository can belong to the same product. Their shared product rules should not need two competing copies. Keep a root `AGENTS.md` for the shared rules and a project `AGENTS.md` for the specifics; they supplement each other rather than replace each other. When two rules genuinely conflict, write down the resolution instead of leaving an agent to pick one.

nodes.name: Give agents a predictable place to look.
nodes.text: ## Give agents a predictable place to look.

nodes.name: Agents work best when the answer to “where is the…
nodes.text: Agents work best when the answer to “where is the guidance?” never changes. Memory files sync to a default local folder, `.nulldull/`, and folders can carry a preferred repository and path so people and agents put files in the same place. Pulling a file never overwrites your local edits.

nodes.name: The CLI’s first-time setup interview helps with existing…
nodes.text: The CLI’s first-time setup interview helps with existing repositories. It scans Markdown file names—never their contents—proposes what to share, asks at most four questions and remembers the answers for that checkout. After that, an agent can start a session by reading the same files a teammate would.

nodes.name: Write for the reader who wasn’t there.
nodes.text: ## Write for the reader who wasn’t there.

nodes.name: The person reading a decision later did not hear the…
nodes.text: The person reading a decision later did not hear the discussion. Neither did the agent. Write the conclusion first, then the reason, then the conditions under which it should be revisited. Name things the way the code and the interface name them, so a search finds the rule.

nodes.name: Short files with one clear owner age better than one long…
nodes.text: Short files with one clear owner age better than one long file that tries to cover everything. If a document starts collecting unrelated rules, split it and link the parts. An agent asked to follow “the deployment rules” does better with one file called that than with a paragraph buried in a general overview.

nodes.name: Make updates part of the work.
nodes.text: ## Make updates part of the work.

nodes.name: When a decision changes, update the document that owns it.…
nodes.text: When a decision changes, update the document that owns it. Link to supporting details instead of copying entire sections into every file. Review a proposed edit against the current version.

nodes.name: Memory is built around that process: versioned Markdown,…
nodes.text: Memory is built around that process: versioned Markdown, explicit access, and changes that retain their history. Every write names the revision it was based on, so a stale edit fails instead of quietly replacing newer work. It does not make an outdated instruction correct; keeping guidance useful remains a team responsibility. But it makes the current version easy to find and the history easy to follow.
